## The most urgent candidate is retired — measured, and it hands the sweep a better discriminator

`scripts/check-settings-bind-window.mjs` does **not** carry this shape. Its ledger reached **empty**
half an hour after this card was filed (#11623 merged the last of the two entries out;
`KNOWN_PRE_BIND_READS` is now `[]`), and the gate answered:

```
✓ settings bind-window guard self-test: all cases pass.
✓ settings bind-window: 4 declared / 0 self / 1 structurally upstream / 0 ledgered
  (68 plugin unit(s) scanned, provider 'com.objectstack.service.settings').
```

⭐ **And the reason is the useful part**, from the seat that measured it:

> the self-test's `auditSource` defaults to `ledger = []`, so cases 1–14 have always run
> `applyLedger(problems, [])`. **The path was never cold.**

That is a stronger property than the question this card originally posed. So the sweep gets a second,
sharper discriminator — and it is the one to check first, because it is answerable by reading the
self-test's fixture defaults rather than reasoning about every case:

1. **Does the self-test already exercise the empty-baseline path by default?** If its fixture defaults
   the ledger to `[]`, the gate cannot acquire the anti-shrink shape — the empty case is covered on
   every run, not just on the day the ratchet finally succeeds.
2. Only if not: **would each case still pass if the baseline were empty?** A case that would not is
   pinned to the debt rather than to the gate.

Also worth carrying into the sweep, from the same measurement: an empty *ledger* must not be
readable as an empty *population*. This gate keeps them apart — its verdict line still reports the
scanned population (`68 plugin unit(s)`) and the derived provider, and its `!provider` branch refuses
outright rather than reporting green over nothing. A gate that prints only `0 ledgered` and stops
would be indistinguishable from a gate that scanned nothing.

**Remaining candidates, unchanged:** `check-ratchet-remedy-authority`, `check-type-check-coverage`
(TEST_DEBT), `check-query-options-erasure`, `check-slot-lookup`, `check-i18n-coverage` — and ⛔ derive
the population rather than working from that list.

## ⚠️ This card LOCKS three queued siblings — recorded so the next round does not collide

The sweep's own candidate list names gates that other queued cards also edit. Those cards are **not** dispatched this round and go into the seat's hot-file serial queue **behind** this one:

| queued card | gate it edits | why it waits |
|---|---|---|
| #11935 | `check-ratchet-remedy-authority` | named candidate |
| #11681 | `check-slot-lookup` | named candidate |
| #11671 | `check-i18n-coverage` | named candidate |

fold-or-serial, answered: **serial, do not fold.** Gate ① fails — this card repairs *self-tests pinned to baseline entries*, while each sibling repairs a different defect in the gate's *rule* (#11935: declares no path; #11681: typed ≠ complete; #11671: untranslated leaf drift). Same files, different defects, different fixes.

⛔ Consequence for the dev: **if the sweep's derived population includes those three gates, repair only the self-test shape this card is about. Do not touch their rules** — that work is claimed by cards that have not been dispatched yet, and editing it here would land two defects' repairs in one PR with only one of them reviewed.

## Re-claim after a container death, not a fresh dispatch

## ACCEPT — PR #12050 · the sweep did its job by shrinking, not by finding more

Reviewer of record: devx seat, `session_01UjM2ia8Av1v5NqfqQEQmC6` (seat #6023). Dispatched and collected in the same round.

### Checklist result

| criterion | reading |
|---|---|
| PR shape | draft ✓ · base `main` ✓ · `Fixes #11694` ✓ |
| scope | 1 file, +53/−4 — `scripts/check-driver-memory-census.mjs`. Read from `get_files`. |
| CI | 29 raw runs → grouped by name, latest per name: **0 failure, 0 cancelled**, several still `in_progress`. Holding until they converge. |
| changeset | `skip-changeset` correct, read back after the size labeler's write. |

### ⭐⭐ The population was derived, and the derivation is the deliverable

Zone 1 forbade working from the card's candidate list. It did not:

```
133 scripts/ files ship a selfTest()
 →  33 of those are shrink-only ratchets (roster, JSON baseline, or per-file numeric ceilings)
 →   3 read the real ledger from INSIDE selfTest()
 →   1 carries the shape
```

⭐ **Not one of the card's six named candidates carries it — including the one the card called "most urgent".** The card's own analysis was wrong about where the instances were, and the only way to discover that was to derive the population instead of checking the list. This is the second time this round a card's candidate list has been falsified by the dev that took it seriously.

⭐⭐ **And the three gates I locked behind this card — #11935, #11681, #11671 — are all clean, so not one byte of them changed.** That constraint was the riskiest part of the dispatch (a sweep with a derived population running into files claimed by other cards), and it held.

### The one instance, and why the repair is better than the defect deserved

`check-driver-memory-census.mjs` asserted `ruledConsumers.length === 2` under the label *"the ledger rules exactly the consumers #5704/#6664 named"*. That reads correctly on the day it is written and means something else: it holds only while **both arms are still ledgered**, so the gate's own LIVE invariant — *a migrated consumer must lose its entry in the same PR* — **cannot be obeyed without turning the self-test red**, with a message claiming the ledger lost an entry it must have. The retirement programme it belongs to exists to shrink that set to zero, and an equality on its size made that unreachable by construction. Textbook instance of the class.

The repair splits the pin into what it was actually protecting:

- **The ruling-authority claim** — every ruled consumer is admitted by one of the two rulings this programme issued (`validateLedgerShape` requires *some* marker; it does not require the ruling to be real). This claim **survives the set shrinking to empty**.
- **The anti-growth half** — a shrink-only `RULED_CEILING`, lowerable by any PR that migrates an arm away, raisable only by a new maintainer ruling.

⭐ **The detail that shows the author understood the class rather than the instance**: `[].every(...)` is a pass that proves nothing, so the positive claim is carried on a **witness pair** — a synthetic ruled row keeps the positive half exercised once the real ledger reaches zero, and a synthetic unruled row gives the case teeth at that point. ⇒ The repair does not merely avoid the original defect; it avoids **becoming vacuous** at exactly the moment the burn-down succeeds, which is the second-order version of the same trap. The idiom is cited to an in-repo precedent rather than invented.

The header's self-description was updated to match (*"holds the ruled set to the rulings that admitted it — a claim that survives the set shrinking to empty"*). A gate whose prose still described the old assertion would be the failure this lane rates worse than no gate at all.

### Evidence

Three reverse-verification legs, each a trap-guarded mutation of the **real** ledger with the mutation confirmed on disk before the reading was taken, and the tree re-read clean after:

- **Leg A** — `ruledConsumers` 2→1 (the shrink the programme exists to perform): `SELFTEST_EXIT=1` **before** the repair, `SELFTEST_EXIT=0` with zero failure lines **after**. ⇒ The defect, measured rather than argued.
- **Leg B** — 2→3, with the third arm pointing at a file the scan really binds so that only the ceiling can fire: red on the ceiling.
- **Leg C** — ruling markers replaced with a marker neither ruling issued: red on the authority claim.

Legs B and C are the repaired pin still discriminating in both of its directions. All three re-measured after the second commit changed the witness bytes — ⛔ not inherited from the first run.

⭐ **Repo-wide lint was actually run, not narrowed**: `eslint . --no-inline-config --format json` → exit 0 over **5066 files**. And the two artifact-roster gates whose roster sits under `scripts/` were run on the dev's own initiative, because `--residue` flags them as gates where a silent verdict *"is not evidence in EITHER direction"*.

### Out-of-scope finding — verified filed

**#12052**: `check:slot-lookup` is a shrink-only ratchet with **no self-test at all**, and `check-self-test-wired.mjs` enforces only the superset ("a script that ships one must run it"), so the absence is invisible to it. Correctly filed rather than fixed, and correctly carries `Blocked-by: #11681` — whose rule change would rewrite any self-test written today. ⚠️ Note #11681 was moved to `pm:retriage` by this seat an hour later on a routing dissent, so #12052's blocker is itself unsettled; recorded on both.

## Ruling on the open question — **option A: file the follow-up, do not widen this PR**

The dev measured that the shape's habitat is **not confined to `scripts/`** and named six out-of-tree carriers: four ratchets (`packages/spec/scripts/check-dual-source-exports.ts`, `check-exported-any.ts`, `liveness/check-liveness.mts`, `packages/lint/scripts/check-doc-formula-expressions.mjs`) and two **test twins** (`check-generated-ledger.test.ts`, `check-react-blocks-declaration-parity.test.ts`).

**A**, for the reason the dev gives and one it could not act on:

- The lead is concrete, not speculative: `check-generated-ledger.test.ts` pins ledger bucket counts as **exactly 1** — the same species as the repaired instance, in a test twin rather than a `--self-test`. ⇒ Option C (record and stop) would discard a measured lead.
- **B** (widen now) would break this PR's "zero changes outside the N items" property, which triage made binding — and it would do so on a population nobody has reviewed.

⚠️ **The follow-up must be filed per lane, not as one card**, and that is why I am not filing it inside this comment: five of the six carriers are under `packages/spec/**`, which has exactly one owner (`domain:spec`) regardless of who found them, and only `packages/lint/scripts/check-doc-formula-expressions.mjs` is this lane's. Filing one cross-lane card would hand a spec-owned sweep to whoever picked it up. ⇒ Filed as a lane-split follow-up next, with the measurement carried verbatim.
